scenes.title: The Ride Up
scenes.setup: Late afternoon. The four strangers (the mother with her two kids) ride up in one of Table Mountain's round Swiss-made Rotair cable cars. The floor slowly turns so everyone gets the 360-degree view: Cape Town's city bowl, Lion's Head, Signal Hill, Robben Island in Table Bay, the Atlantic glittering. The sheer sandstone cliff slides past the windows. Nobody knows anyone yet.

lines.speaker: mechanic
lines.say: Ain't this view somethin', huh? Bet nothin' I fixed beats that.
lines.gesture: leans against the side, arms crossed
lines.thought: I want to be noticed here.

lines.speaker: lucky
lines.say: Oi, Javier! This view? It’s like winning the lottery without a ticket! Nha amigu, isn’t that somethin'?
lines.gesture: gesturing towards the view with a big smile
lines.thought: I love making others laugh, even with no luck in my pocket.

lines.speaker: mom
lines.say: Yeah, but I'd trade this view for a full inhaler any day.
lines.thought: His asthma's got me on high alert.

lines.speaker: lucky
lines.say: Tsk, tsk, Maggie! Life's a mountain, not just a view, you sabe?
lines.gesture: grinning and pointing at the view
lines.thought: I love making light when others worry.

lines.speaker: mom
lines.say: Milo, sure, it’s pretty, but these kids need my focus.
lines.gesture: glance at my son with the inhaler
lines.thought: Their safety comes first, no matter the view.

scenes.summary: Javier and Milo admire the breathtaking view, with Javier claiming it surpasses anything he's fixed, while Milo likens it to winning the lottery. Maggie interrupts their enthusiasm, expressing her priority for her kids over the scenery. Javier feels proud of his work, Milo is exhilarated by the beauty, and Maggie is anxious about her responsibilities.

scenes.title: Last Car Down
scenes.setup: Golden hour on the summit. The south-easter has come up fast and the white 'tablecloth' cloud is pouring over the edge. A loudspeaker crackles: the wind is closing the cableway, this is the LAST car down, everyone aboard now. The four of them (and the kids) are the last passengers. The attendant waves them all in, even the one without a ticket. The doors seal. The car swings out over the cliff.

lines.speaker: mechanic
lines.say: Last car down, huh? Let's make sure we don't get stuck up here, boss.
lines.thought: Gotta keep control in this situation.

lines.speaker: scholar
lines.say: Javier, I can’t even look down right now. This is too much!
lines.thought: What if the cable snaps? I'm so scared.

lines.speaker: mechanic
lines.say: Listen, Aaliyah, you gotta trust the ride. It'll hold up, ain't that right, Milo?
lines.thought: I want her to feel safe, taking charge here.

lines.speaker: mom
lines.say: Hey, hold my hand, kid. We’re gonna be fine.
lines.thought: I need to keep them safe, no matter what.

lines.speaker: lucky
lines.say: Ah, don’t worry, Aaliyah! This car has seen worse! Nha amigu, let's enjoy the ride!
lines.gesture: waves hand dismissively with a grin
lines.thought: Just another funny story waiting to happen!

scenes.summary: Javier reassures Aaliyah about the ride while trying to keep her calm. Maggie encourages Milo to hold her hand, and Milo tries to comfort Aaliyah about the safety of the car. Aaliyah feels anxious and scared, Javier is somewhat confident, Maggie feels protective, and Milo is optimistic.

scenes.title: Halfway
scenes.setup: Halfway down the cliff, with a bang and a lurch, the car stops dead. The lights die. The drive has lost power and the car hangs swinging over a 400-metre drop, the city lights coming on far below. The operator is out of contact. The wind is getting worse. They are on their own.

lines.speaker: scholar
lines.say: We can't just hang here! We need to open the hatch and check the motor now.
lines.thought: If we wait too long, the wind could become unbearable.

lines.speaker: mechanic
lines.say: Listen up, Aaliyah. I’m opening that hatch now. Hold tight!
lines.thought: We can't waste time; I need to take charge.
lines.outcome: Javier works on the roof hatch: progress on the roof hatch (47%)

lines.speaker: mom
lines.say: Javier, I need you to hurry. He's almost out!
lines.thought: His inhaler can't run out tonight.

lines.say: The wind howls harder. Wind 8/10.
The 7-year-old starts wheezing hard. His mother digs for the inhaler: it's nearly empty.

lines.speaker: lucky
lines.say: Aaliyah, I’ll help with the little one! Just breathe, pequeno!
lines.thought: Keeping the boy calm is crucial; I have to make him smile.
lines.outcome: Milo works on the boy's asthma: progress on the boy's asthma (45%)

lines.speaker: mom
lines.say: Javier, keep working! I need you to just get that hatch open!
lines.thought: My kid's health comes first, no delay.

lines.speaker: mechanic
lines.say: I ain't stoppin' now, Aaliyah! This hatch's comin' open, trust me.
lines.gesture: yanks at the hatch with determination
lines.thought: I need to show I’m in charge.
lines.outcome: Javier works on the roof hatch: the roof hatch: DONE

lines.say: A violent gust slams the cabin sideways. Wind 9/10.

lines.speaker: lucky
lines.say: Aaliyah, don't worry! Just breathe with me, okay? Nha amigu!
lines.thought: Keeping the kid calm could save him.
lines.outcome: Milo works on the boy's asthma: progress on the boy's asthma (77%)

lines.speaker: scholar
lines.say: Javier, remember the wind speeds! We need to fix the motor before it reaches 10!
lines.thought: I can't let my fear stop me from helping.

lines.speaker: mom
lines.say: Javier, get that motor going now! Time's running out!
lines.thought: The wind won't wait for us.

lines.say: A violent gust slams the cabin sideways. Wind 10/10.

scenes.summary: Aaliyah urged the group to check the motor, while Javier confidently opened the roof hatch despite the worsening conditions. Milo assisted with the boy's asthma as Maggie pressed Javier to hurry with the motor fix before it was too late. Aaliyah feels anxious about the situation, Javier is determined but under pressure, Maggie is frantic with concern, and Milo remains supportive and focused on the boy's needs. Outcome: No motor, no signal. They hung in the dark all night, and at dawn, when the wind dropped, the cableway crew winched the car down. The boy's breathing got worse through the night; paramedics were waiting at the bottom. Milo worked on the boy's asthma. Javier worked on the roof hatch. Aaliyah and Maggie never managed to make a difference.

scenes.title: After
scenes.setup: The night is over, one way or another. stepping out of the cabin at dawn, stiff and cold.

lines.speaker: scholar
lines.say: I can't believe we survived that. Did we really help anyone?
lines.thought: I'm overwhelmed by my failure to help.
lines.where: stepping out of the cabin at dawn, stiff and cold

lines.speaker: lucky
lines.say: Ah, Aaliyah, we survived like true champions, sabe? That's somethin' to celebrate!
lines.gesture: spreading arms wide with a grin
lines.thought: I want to lift her spirits.
lines.where: stepping out of the cabin at dawn, stiff and cold

lines.speaker: mechanic
lines.say: Help? We almost lost the kid, but we made it out, boss.
lines.thought: I need to prove I'm in charge.
lines.where: stepping out of the cabin at dawn, stiff and cold

lines.speaker: mom
lines.say: Almost lost him, and we did nothing? That's not celebration, Milo.
lines.thought: This isn't just survival; it's about my kid's health.
lines.where: stepping out of the cabin at dawn, stiff and cold

ending.title: Dawn on the Wire
lines: No motor, no signal. They hung in the dark all night, and at dawn, when the wind dropped, the cableway crew winched the car down.
The boy's breathing got worse through the night; paramedics were waiting at the bottom.
Milo worked on the boy's asthma.
Javier worked on the roof hatch.
Aaliyah and Maggie never managed to make a difference.
